question.text: This early 19th century Zulu monarch developed the "bull horn" formation and a shorter style of spear as part of his massive military reformation. The expansion of his realm is argued to have triggered the Mfecane (m-fay-thaa-nay), a long period of social upheaval in southern Africa.
question.clue: This man ordered the milk in his empire to be drained away after the death of his mother Nandi; after Nandi's death, this ruler massacred over 7,000 of his own subjects which led his brother Dingane to assassinate him.

swap.leadin: This policy was reinforced by the Bantu Education Act.
swap.text: Name this policy, which Stephen Biko protested in South Africa. It called for the racial segregation of blacks and whites.
swap.clue: It became harsher during Hendrik Verwoerd's prime ministership with the creation of ten Bantustan "homelands."

question.text: While leading the African National Congress, Mandela became the first Black leader of this country.
question.clue: In that song, musicians pledged to not play at a casino resort in this country, "Sun City".

swap.leadin: This empire was once ruled by Tunka Manin, and its demise brought the rise of the Sosso people.
swap.text: Name this empire which had its capital at Koumbi-Saleh and gives its name to a modern day country with capital at Accra.
swap.clue: This empire reached its height around 1100, and some claimed that it had a 200,000 man-army.

question.leadin: -give these answers related to countries no longer on the map.
question.text: In 1964 the African countries of Tanganyika [TAN-guh-NEE-kah] and Zanzibar merged to form this country whose name incorporates syllables from both predecessors.
question.clue: In 1998, this country and Kenya suffered bombings at their U.S. embassies.

swap.text: Third in length to the Nile and Congo, this West African river is the namesake of two of the countries it flows through. It was the principal river of the Mali, Ghana, and Songhay Empires.
swap.clue: In the 1990s, the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People, or MOSOP, was founded by Ken Saro-Wiwa to protest the exploitation of the oil resources of this river's delta.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about an African empire.
question.text: This empire had its capital at Gao, and its first great king Sonni Ali repressed the scholars of Timbuktu.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Polynesian expansion of the 1st millennium.
swap.text: This island country was settled by Polynesians who are the ancestors of its Merina people. This country's modern people are the descendants of those Polynesians and Bantu migrants from its mainland.
swap.clue: A rebellion on this island named for the red shawls of its participants was put down by Joseph Gallieni.

question.leadin: This man became regent of his country by engineering the downfall of Lij Yasu.
question.text: Name this ruler whose power was subsumed by a junta called the Derg. Opposition to his rule was concentrated in the breakaway state of Eritrea.
question.answerHtml: Haile Selassie I [or Power of the Trinity; or Ras Tafari Makonnen]
question.clue: When his country was invaded by a European power, he made his headquarters at Desse, but after losing a battle at Maychew he was forced to flee.

swap.text: This Igbo-led breakaway state in southeastern Nigeria lost a bloody civil war in the late 1960s, during which Doctors Without Borders was founded.
swap.clue: A blockade of this country led to the largest civilian aid airlift in world history to alleviate starvation.

question.leadin: The Lari Massacre occurred during this conflict, and leaders of it include Waruhiu Itote and Dedan Kimathi.
question.text: Name this uprising against British colonial rule which began in 1952.
question.clue: Rawson Macharia was a key witness at the trial of the Kapenguria Six, who were convicted during this conflict.

swap.leadin: A European trade war in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries here led to the unique geographies of some African nations.
swap.text: Name this country, formerly a British colony, located on a namesake river and with capital Banjul.
swap.clue: Operation Restore Democracy was a military intervention by ECOWAS in this country in January. It occurred because this country's President Yahya Jammeh refused to step down to make room for Adama Barrow. This country's capital is Banjul and it lies on either side of its namesake river.

question.text: Scottish Presbyterians founded schools in Blantyre for this colony's Chewa people, who attended Salisbury's university during its federation with Rhodesia. John Chilembwe created this colony's Providence Industrial Mission.
question.answerHtml: Nyasaland [or Nyasaland Protectorate; accept Malawi or Republic of Malawi or Dziko la Malaŵi or Charu cha Malaŵi; accept Maravi Empire or Kingdom of Maravi; accept Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland or University College of Rhodesia and Nyasaland]

swap.leadin: According to al-Umari, the central participant of this event did not want to meet with the Mamluk sultan al-Malik al-Nasir because he would be obligated to kiss the ground and the sultan's hand.
swap.text: Name this event, during which a ruler of the Mali Empire devastated the economy of Cairo for twelve years through his generosity by giving out and spending a massive amount of gold.
swap.answerHtml: Mansa Musa’s hajj [or Mansa Musa’s pilgrimage to Mecca, or anything indicating Mansa Musa going to Mecca; prompt on partial answers]
swap.clue: Some architects who returned from this event helped build new structures in Gao.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the ongoing Arab Spring uprisings.
question.text: This Tunisian fruit vendor is said to have set off the Arab Spring protests when he lit himself on fire out of exasperation on December 17, 2010.
question.clue: This street vendor who self-immolated in 2010 after continued harassment by the police. Pro-democracy protests broke out in Tunisia after this man's self-immolation.

swap.leadin: Ritual flogging was a key portion of the yondo ritual that Francois Tombalbaye ("tohm-bahl-BYE") forced his people to undergo as part of a program with this name.
swap.text: Give this French-language term also used by Mobutu Sese Seko. This term describes the process of changing personal and place names to reject Western influence.
swap.clue: This policy, which also supported the "Three Z's" of "Our Country, Our River, Our Money." This policy renamed the Stanley Pool to the Malebo Pool, amongst other localizations.

question.text: This founder of the National Union of Popular Forces, a leftist party in Morocco, disappeared in Paris in 1965. Ronen Bergman's 2018 book Rise and Kill First alleges that he was killed in a Mossad safe house by Moroccan intelligence operatives and French police officers.

swap.leadin: This man's victory at the Battle of Dulmadobe in 1913 led to reprisals such as the 1920 bombing of Taalex.
swap.text: Name this poet-warrior who fought British, Italian, and Ethiopian forces on behalf of his "dervish state" of Salihiyah Muslims.
swap.answerHtml: the “Mad Mullah” [or Sayyid Maxamed Cabdulle Xasan; or Mohammed Abdullah Hassan]
swap.clue: This man died unceremoniously of influenza in Ogaden after the Royal Air Force bombarded his capital at Taleh with impunity since his followers thought the planes were the chariots of Allah planning to take them up to heaven.

question.text: This king of Dahomey overthrew his brother Adandozan with the help of Portugese slaver Francisco Felix de Sousa. This man long resisted British attempts to force an end to the Dahomey slave trade, and his many personal slaves included Sara Forbes Bonetta, who later became a goddaughter of Queen Victoria.

swap.leadin: A leader of this movement composed a poem on the death of the colonial police officer Richard Corfield, instructing Corfield on the story he should tell in Hell.
swap.text: Name this anti-colonial, pro-Islamic resistance movement in British Somaliland. This movement enacted a short-lived namesake state under the warrior-poet Mohammed Abdallah Hassan, whom the British called the "Mad Mullah."
